Explicit Legendre root differences give the complete 1–3-node resonance sets. For four nodes, a simultaneous resonance would make the ratio of the outer and inner positive roots rational, contradicting its squared value (23+4 sqrt(30))/7. The undamped Rayleigh quotient along the continued-fraction subsequence is at most pi^2/q_k^2; trace one then gives the stated condition bound. Direct integration yields the exact continuous eigenvalues and the normalized operator-norm error limit. The standalone verifier executed 163 assertions from the actual candidate package path. value.rationale: The smallest all-step rank-safe positive Gaussian quadrature is a natural efficiency/robustness target for finite-horizon covariance and controllability computations. The result distinguishes positivity, strict positivity, and uniform conditioning; it exhibits an all-step rank-safe quadrature that becomes arbitrarily ill-conditioned and asymptotically fails to approximate a well-conditioned normalized continuous Gramian. These distinctions matter for reliability of finite-horizon Gramian computation. The precise Gauss-node arithmetic and inverse-square subsequence are not arbitrary parameter slices.
